submission.justification: Recommend Radiator-R2 at the maximum allowed thickness, 6 cm. Radiator-R3 is the nominally highest-index candidate and would be attractive for photon yield, but it fails the non-replaceable lifetime humidity requirement with 40% transparency loss. Of the two ageing-compliant options, R2 has only 6% transparency loss and is the porous/higher-yield option relative to the lower-index R1, so it is the best feasible choice for maximizing 10 GeV/c pion/kaon separation. Choosing 6 cm maximizes Cherenkov photon statistics within the allowed 1–6 cm range and therefore gives the strongest separation for the compliant radiator set.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c.
requirements.evidence: R3 is rejected by the hard ageing constraint; between the compliant candidates, R2 is the porous radiator while R1 is lower-index, so R2 at maximum allowed thickness gives the best feasible photon statistics and separation.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md lists Radiator-R1, Radiator-R2, and Radiator-R3; the recommendation is Radiator-R2.

requirements.requirement: The pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c must be at least 3.5 sigma.
requirements.evidence: The selected configuration uses the best feasible radiator after excluding the humidity-failing R3 and the maximum allowed thickness to maximize photon yield; this is the configuration chosen to satisfy the 3.5 sigma separation target.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after a 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%.
requirements.evidence: ageing_tests.md reports Radiator-R2 transparency loss at 400 nm of 6%, below the 10% maximum. R3 has 40% and is rejected; R1 has 3% but lower expected separation.
Recommended thickness is 6 cm, which is within the allowed range.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended radiator and thickness.
